newsitem.title: CHINA: China stocks rebound despite crackdown rumours.
newsitem.headline: China stocks rebound despite crackdown rumours.

text.p: China's stock markets rebounded on Thursday after a sharp two-day fall, bolstered by optimism that a possible government crackdown on market speculation could standardise and stabilise trading, analysts said.

Investors widely expect a leadership reshuffling in the securities sector and punishment of several major brokerages for trading infractions, but many expect the overall market to benefit from the outcome, they said.
On Thursday, Shanghai's foreign currency B share index jumped ahead by 1.44 percent to end at 88.77 points and its Shenzhen counterpart added 1.05 percent to 172.53.
On the domestic share markets, the Shanghai A share index leaped 2.82 percent to 1,483.243 and Shenzhen's A index gained a solid 3.09 percent to 515.47.
Chinese brokers reported speculation that Beijing may soon ban several major brokerages from conducting securities trading on their own account and remove its top securities regulator.

The chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), Zhou Daojiong, was expected to step down soon and an announcement was likely within days, they said. CSRC officials have declined to comment.
Zhou, appointed in 1995, was expected to be replaced by Zhou Zhengqing, current chairman of the Securities Commission under the State Council, or cabinet, brokers said.
Share indices on China's two stock markets have surged more than 50 percent so far this year despite repeated warnings from Beijing about overheating.

"Many investors believe the measures will benefit the market in the long run," said an A share trader. "Market fundamentals, in particular the improvement of the national economy and performance of listed firms, support a continued bull run."
"The most important point is that in the past year, Beijing has made clear that it is determined to expand and develop the markets," said an executive at a major Chinese brokerage.

"A year ago, whenever there was market talk about a crackdown, fears over closure of the markets emerged," he added. "But now clampdown measures are very much viewed as necessary to standardise and stabilise the markets."

Brokers said at least four brokerages, including Shenyin & Wanguo Securities, China's largest brokerage, would be barred from conducting trading on their own account as punishment for irregularities, including trading on credit.
Others rumoured to be involved include Shanghai-based Haitong Securities and Guangdong-based J&A Securities and Guangfa Securities.
Officials at the firms declined to comment on the speculation.
Several sources said the brokerages had been informed of the decision but had been given a grace period to appeal.
On Thursday, Huangshan Tourism Development Co was the biggest gainer on the Shanghai B share market, rising $0.07 or 7.95 percent to $0.95 on volume of 794,100 shares.
On the Shenzhen B market, Shenzhen Fangda Industry Co was the biggest gainer, rising HK$0.79 or 6.63 percent to HK$12.70 on volume of 670,860 shares.
